headline: LLMs Explain Unfamiliar Code and save developers hours of manual analysis
summary: A new tool leverages Large Language Models to parse and document codebases, eliminating the need for manual deciphering of legacy logic.
details: Ever been handed a massive chunk of unfamiliar code and asked to explain its functionality, especially an obscure edge case? This is a common developer pain point, often leading to hours spent reverse-engineering undocumented functions and legacy logic.

Manual code spelunking is tedious and time-consuming. Fortunately, a new approach utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate this process. The tool parses your codebase, analyzes symbol relations and call graphs, and generates structured documentation and explanations.

Simply configure your LLM settings and run the tool against your target directory. It then analyzes the code to produce clear, detailed explanations, freeing developers from deciphering every line themselves.

This approach can significantly reduce the time spent on understanding and documenting code written by others. The project also supports advanced configurations, multiple languages/parsers, caching, and various engine options, with contributions and feedback always welcome.
caption:
Tired of explaining code you didn't write? LLMs can now do the heavy lifting for you.

Ever been handed a massive chunk of unfamiliar code and asked to explain its functionality, especially an obscure edge case? This is a common developer pain point, often leading to hours spent reverse-engineering undocumented functions and legacy logic.

Manual code spelunking is tedious and time-consuming. Fortunately, a new approach utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate this process. The tool parses your codebase, analyzes symbol relations and call graphs, and generates structured documentation and explanations.

Simply configure your LLM settings and run the tool against your target directory. It then analyzes the code to produce clear, detailed explanations, freeing developers from deciphering every line themselves.

This approach can significantly reduce the time spent on understanding and documenting code written by others. The project also supports advanced configurations, multiple languages/parsers, caching, and various engine options, with contributions and feedback always welcome.
